verdict.rationale: Lium's own docs describe clusters as several whole machines on the same RDMA fabric for one distributed job, which covers the multi-node and fast-interconnect core. The no-sales-cycle part is only implied by general self-serve features (signup with no email, card billing, renting via API) that are documented for pods, not specifically for clusters. missing for 10: a documented self-serve cluster provisioning flow (CLI/API/console), cluster sizes and interconnect specs, explicit confirmation that clusters need no sales contact, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can provision a multi-node GPU cluster with fast interconnect for distributed training without a sales cycle

citations.quote: A cluster is several whole machines on the same RDMA fabric, for one distributed job.
An agent can do everything on Lium with no browser: sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods.
fingerprint signup: one call to `POST /auth/signup`, no email, no password, no confirmation link.
Pay by card, US bank debit (ACH), crypto, TAO or alpha.
